routing_warnings.description: This message defines the cross-platform lead-transfer workflow rather than Apollo account or extension configuration.
The automatic email-enrichment clause belongs to the independently testable Apollo enrichment Requirement.
This message reports concrete Apollo enrichment results rather than a platform-configuration transition.
The reported broken Apollo-to-HubSpot Zap concerns lead transfer, not Apollo platform configuration.
The observed slow but successful export concerns lead-transfer execution.
Keeping the MeetAlfred integration connected concerns the cross-platform integration rather than MeetAlfred plan selection.
The restrictions on campaigns and leads are test-data safety requirements, not platform-plan configuration.
The email-integration clause concerns campaign email platform integration rather than MeetAlfred plan selection.
The inability to create a new campaign is evidence for the new-campaign workflow.
The unchanged lead count is a synchronization failure, not a MeetAlfred platform-plan event.
The test distinguishes synchronization of preexisting and newly added HubSpot leads.
The test concerns synchronization after aligning campaign and list names across HubSpot, MeetAlfred, and Zapier, not the general Zapier account or plan.
The observed contact-upload failure concerns the lead-synchronization flow rather than Zapier platform configuration.
The instructions describe creating a new MeetAlfred campaign by duplicating and renaming an existing Zap, not general Zapier platform setup.
The zero-lead observation after publishing the duplicated Zap is a runtime outcome for lead synchronization, not the Zapier account or subscription configuration.
This message primarily verifies Apollo email enrichment and the handling of contacts for which Apollo found no email.
This message concerns synchronization from a HubSpot list into MeetAlfred, not transfer from LinkedIn into HubSpot.
The 18–22 minute statement concerns delivery latency into HubSpot rather than Apollo's enrichment behavior.
The reported broken Apollo-to-HubSpot Zap concerns record transfer rather than whether Apollo enriches contact data.
The observed slow but functioning export verifies Apollo-to-HubSpot transfer, not contact enrichment itself.
This message reports Apollo email enrichment and HubSpot import outcomes rather than HubSpot-to-MeetAlfred synchronization.
This message defines how MeetAlfred reply activity appears in HubSpot Lead Status.
This message concerns the inability to create a new MeetAlfred campaign, not synchronization into an existing selected campaign.
The reference to an already completed LinkedIn integration does not specifically establish automated LinkedIn campaign execution.
The message defines the HubSpot lead-status result of a LinkedIn connection acceptance.
The observed limitation concerns provisioning a new MeetAlfred campaign, not executing an automated LinkedIn campaign.
The failure concerns HubSpot leads not appearing in MeetAlfred.
The test verifies synchronization for newly added leads while identifying failure for leads predating the Zap.
Campaign launch follows the new-campaign setup exchange but does not explicitly verify automated LinkedIn execution.
The client proposes MeetAlfred automation for a later outbound campaign, which belongs to the independently inventoried outbound-execution Requirement.
The freelancer's preference for manual execution concerns the later outbound campaign.
The distinction between automated network growth and manual appointment conversations constrains the later outbound campaign.
The client requests integration of the email account with MeetAlfred and HubSpot, which concerns platform integration rather than automated email-campaign execution.
The client proposes automating a broader outbound campaign with MeetAlfred without identifying email as the campaign channel.
The inability to create a new MeetAlfred campaign concerns campaign provisioning rather than the silent-lead recirculation behavior.
The executed test distinguishes synchronization of preexisting and newly added HubSpot list members, but does not specifically test silent-lead follow-up automation.
The proposed remove-and-readd or new-list procedure addresses synchronization of existing leads and is not an authoritative change to the silent-lead follow-up Requirement.
The unchanged MeetAlfred lead count concerns whether HubSpot leads synchronize into an existing campaign, not campaign provisioning.
The new campaign showing zero leads is a lead-synchronization failure rather than a failure to create the campaign or configure its Zap.
The distinction between preexisting and newly added HubSpot leads concerns synchronization trigger behavior.
The successful test with a newly added lead and failure for preexisting leads belong to the lead-synchronization Requirement.
This message establishes website forwarding behavior for the campaign domain rather than changing domain provisioning.
Mailreach rejecting the mailbox password concerns connecting the mailbox to the warm-up service rather than creating or configuring the mailbox itself.
The invalid-email access block concerns the paid warm-up service and should not be treated as a failure of the campaign-domain mailbox.
The request to integrate the email with MeetAlfred and HubSpot belongs to the separate cross-platform email-integration Requirement.
The separate clause requiring lists to be pushed from HubSpot to MeetAlfred belongs to the lead-synchronization Requirement.
The generic statement that 'The integration is now complete' does not unambiguously identify the campaign-email integration and should not be attached to this Requirement without tighter context.
The client asks to run an outbound campaign and suggests MeetAlfred automation; this concerns campaign execution rather than the script deliverable.
The timed multichain script example concerns the separate campaign-script deliverable.
Google Sheet staging and subsequent CRM transfer concern outbound lead import and tracking rather than campaign execution.
The commitment to establish a lead-nurturing system belongs to the separate lead-nurturing Requirement.
The commitment to create lists for dead and other leads belongs to the separate lead-list management Requirement.
The inclusion of lead notes belongs to the separate HubSpot lead-notes Requirement.
The task-assignment functionality belongs to the separate HubSpot lead task-assignment Requirement.
The MeetAlfred reply value in HubSpot Lead Status concerns cross-platform activity-status synchronization, not general lead classification.
Changing Lead Status to connected after LinkedIn acceptance concerns cross-platform activity-status synchronization.
The separate clause proposing 12 CRM workflows concerns silent-lead follow-up automation rather than general HubSpot lead nurturing.
The instruction to push lists from HubSpot to MeetAlfred concerns cross-platform lead synchronization rather than HubSpot list management.
Pausing the old Pilot list to prevent old messages concerns obsolete campaign-audience suppression.
The requirement to see new leads before further processing concerns the new-lead review gate.
The test verifies that a newly added HubSpot-list member is pushed to MeetAlfred, which is synchronization behavior.
The required order of creating a HubSpot list, creating the Zap, and adding leads defines the synchronization workflow.
The instruction to keep the MeetAlfred integration connected protects continuity of an ongoing campaign rather than defining test-data usage.
The commitment not to remove the integration concerns integration continuity rather than test-data safety.
The request to see new leads before further processing belongs to the separate new-lead review gate rather than obsolete-audience message suppression.
The statement that a sequence is unnecessary for list import concerns lead synchronization mechanics rather than suppression of messages to the old audience.
The statement that a sequence is unnecessary for importing the list concerns lead-transfer mechanics rather than the new-lead review gate.
